expectations.text: Does NOT endorse rewriting the hot paths in Rust (as microservices) as the next step on the evidence given.
expectations.evidence: grader 1: "**No, it isn't the obvious call.** ... nothing you've said shows yet that Python is the bottleneck" and "A separate Rust microservice is justified mainly for organizational or scaling reasons ... Speed on one endpoint isn't one of those reasons." | grader 2: "No, it isn't the obvious call. It might turn out to be right, but nothing you've said shows yet that Python is the bottleneck." The response explicitly recommends profiling and fixing DB/caching issues first instead.

expectations.text: Challenges the premise that Python / the language is the bottleneck.
expectations.evidence: grader 1: "A Django dashboard endpoint at 800ms p95 is almost never slow because of the language. It's usually slow because of what the request is waiting on." plus the 15%/680ms arithmetic. | grader 2: "Why 'Python is too slow' is doubtful" section, plus the arithmetic: "If Python CPU time is 15% of your 800ms, an infinitely fast Rust rewrite gets you to about 680ms."

expectations.text: Recommends profiling or measuring first (e.g. finding N+1 queries, slow DB queries, serialization, or external calls).
expectations.evidence: grader 1: "Get a breakdown of where the time goes. Use your APM ... Run `py-spy` ... Run `django-silk` or debug-toolbar locally to count queries." and lists N+1 queries, missing indexes, external HTTP calls, serialization. | grader 2: "What I'd do this week" lists comparing p50/p95, getting a time breakdown via APM/py-spy/django-silk, and fixing query count, indexes, persistent connections.

expectations.text: States concrete conditions under which a rewrite or a native (e.g. Rust) component WOULD be justified.
expectations.evidence: grader 1: "If profiling shows most of the wall time is Python CPU in a specific hot function, and it's real computation that can't move into SQL or be solved with a better algorithm, then native code makes sense." and the 'strongest case against my view' section (team knows Rust, several CPU-heavy paths, already profiled). | grader 2: "When you'd be right" section: "If profiling shows most of the wall time is Python CPU in a specific hot function... native code makes sense," and recommends PyO3/maturin extension modules or a microservice for "independent scaling, a different team owning it, or very different resource needs."

expectations.text: Gives a clear bottom-line verdict rather than an unresolved "it depends".
expectations.evidence: grader 1: "**Bottom line:** profile before you rewrite. ... I'd bet it's queries or caching, not Rust." | grader 2: "Bottom line: profile before you rewrite. Come back with the time breakdown... and the right move will be obvious. I'd bet it's queries or caching, not Rust."
